Shift requirements for gate calls for new staff
This page shows new staff a habit of care

Shift requirements at the Companion Animal Travel Desk matter because every gate call can affect a traveler, a pet, and the cabin team at once. Your job is to keep the desk steady, clear, and calm so each handoff goes smoothly. Start by checking the booking notes, then read any welfare comments before you speak with anyone. If the file is thin, ask the senior coordinator for direction rather than guessing. That habit protects service and keeps the record clean.

When you answer a gate call, use simple language and listen for signs that the traveler needs extra help. A pet may be resting, restless, or sensitive to noise, and that changes how you guide the next step. The welfare coordinator may add comfort needs that must be shared with the cabin team without delay. Keep your notes plain and exact, and write only what another staff member needs to continue the work. Do not crowd the record with side remarks, because a clear page helps the next person act fast.

You also need to watch for changes at the gate, since boarding order, carrier checks, and escort needs can shift without warning. If a traveler arrives unsure or upset, stay patient and give one calm instruction at a time. If you see a mismatch between the booking and the animal, pause the handoff and alert the senior coordinator. Good desk work is not only about speed; it is about catching small issues before they grow.

Use the desk log to show what was seen, what was said, and what was passed along. Keep the tone even, the facts short, and the path of care easy to follow. Remember that careful records support safe travel for every animal and every traveler.
